CanEnchantCardType.maps_to: RoyallyApprovedEnchantment.can_enchant (sts2_rl/enchantments.py) -- `super().can_enchant(card) and card.card_type in (CardType.ATTACK, CardType.SKILL)`. RoyallyApproved.cs:16-23 compiles to `(uint)(cardType - 1) <= 1u`, which over CardType's declaration order (None=0, Attack=1, Skill=2, Power=3, Status=4, Curse=5, Quest=6 -- src/Core/Entities/Cards/CardType.cs) is exactly {Attack, Skill}. The sim folds CanEnchantCardType into each subclass's own can_enchant, as every other typed enchantment in the module does. Pinned by test_shared_enchantments.py::test_royally_approved_enchants_attacks_and_skills_only (Strike yes, Defend yes, Inflame no).

OnEnchant.maps_to: RoyallyApprovedEnchantment.modify_card (sts2_rl/enchantments.py) -- sets `card.innate` and `card.retain`, matching RoyallyApproved.cs:25-29's `AddKeyword(CardKeyword.Innate)` + `AddKeyword(CardKeyword.Retain)`. Both are static card properties, so the sim's `modify_card` (EnchantmentModel.ModifyCard -> OnEnchant, EnchantmentModel.cs:355-364) is the right slot: it re-runs wherever the game re-derives a card from its canonical model, which is what keeps a downgrade or a per-combat reset from dropping the keywords. Pinned by test_shared_enchantments.py::test_royally_approved_grants_innate_and_retain.

ExtraHoverTips.rationale: RoyallyApproved.cs:9-14 returns two HoverTipFactory.FromKeyword tips (Innate, Retain). Presentation only, out of scope per the shared contract's presentation waiver -- and redundant with the keywords OnEnchant actually grants.
